patient.chief_complaint: Progressive personality change, impaired judgment, grandiosity — 2 years (wife-reported)
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. W is a 62-year-old former financial advisor who presents with his wife after being referred by his internist for cognitive evaluation. His wife describes a 2-year history of progressive personality changes that have been difficult to separate from his escalating alcohol use. He was terminated from his financial advisory position 18 months ago following several compliance violations — he had been making unauthorized trades in client accounts and dismissing colleagues' concerns about policy violations with dismissive and sometimes belligerent responses. He has never acknowledged that these violations were his fault, insisting he was 'unfairly targeted.' Prior to this, he had a 28-year career without any disciplinary record. At home, he has become increasingly impulsive — making a $30,000 investment in a scheme his wife considers fraudulent, and responding with rage when questioned. He now drinks 4-6 drinks daily by his report; his wife estimates 8-10. He has become grandiose, making claims about his business acumen that are not consistent with his recent performance. He has lost empathy — when his son had a significant health scare, he expressed no concern. He has become highly perseverative in arguments — repeating the same accusations against his former employer in every conversation for 18 months. His sleep apnea is moderate-severe and he abandoned his CPAP after two weeks. He has a family history of possible dementia in his mother (onset her late 50s) and possible psychiatric institutionalization in his maternal uncle. His chronic heavy alcohol use is contributing to his cerebellar signs, and his behavioral changes have unfolded over the same period as the escalation in his drinking.

findings.finding: Markedly impaired. Poor performance on set-shifting (Trail Making Test B), abstraction/similarities, and response inhibition; perseverative errors on Wisconsin-style sorting. Pattern consistent with dorsolateral and orbitofrontal dysfunction.
Reduced letter (phonemic) fluency out of proportion to category fluency — a frontal/executive signature rather than a semantic-store deficit.

Impaired emotion recognition (Ekman faces) and deficits on theory-of-mind / faux-pas tasks, with reduced affective empathy on the Interpersonal Reactivity Index — supports the bvFTD social-cognitive phenotype.
Relatively spared. Encoding and free recall reduced in a dysexecutive (retrieval) pattern, but recognition and cued recall are comparatively preserved.
Preserved. Copy of complex figure and clock contour intact; errors, when present, reflect poor planning rather than a perceptual or constructional deficit.
Fluent with intact single-word comprehension and confrontation naming largely preserved; no agrammatism or semantic loss — argues against a primary progressive aphasia variant.
Reduced insight (anosognosia), stimulus-bound responses, and reduced concern for test performance noted during the session.

Reduced backward digit span (2) with relatively preserved forward span (5), indicating a working-memory/executive rather than a primary attentional deficit. The frontal-executive impairment is the dominant pattern.

The dissociation between impaired executive/social-cognitive performance and preserved memory and visuospatial domains points to selective dysfunction of anterior (frontal-network) cortices

interactions: Naltrexone (alcohol use disorder treatment): hepatic metabolism — mildly elevated liver enzymes do not contraindicate; monthly injections preferred for adherence in bvFTD
Sertraline for bvFTD behavioral symptoms: minimal alcohol interaction; may help disinhibition
contraindications: Disulfiram: avoid in bvFTD — patient may lack impulse control to avoid alcohol, leading to dangerous disulfiram-alcohol reaction
Benzodiazepines for alcohol withdrawal: use with caution in bvFTD — can worsen cognition; use structured CIWA protocol with medical supervision
warnings: Alcohol cessation is CRITICAL — alcohol is actively worsening cerebellar and frontal function AND masking FTD evaluation
Continued alcohol use may prevent meaningful clinical trial eligibility
Thiamine supplementation: oral thiamine 100 mg TID for prophylaxis given low-normal thiamine and heavy alcohol use
alternatives: Inpatient detoxification may be necessary given dependency level
Family-focused alcohol counseling — wife must understand alcohol cessation is part of FTD treatment

results.title: Alcohol use disorder preceding bvFTD diagnosis: a diagnostic challenge

output.summary: In bvFTD, disinhibition and loss of social control can manifest first as escalating alcohol use, which may precede formal FTD diagnosis by years. The FTD-related frontal disinhibition removes the ability to self-regulate drinking behavior, leading to escalating alcohol misuse as an early behavioral symptom. When alcohol use disorder co-occurs with new behavioral disinhibition and social dysfunction, FTD should be considered in the differential. FDG-PET obtained after an abstinence interval has been used in research settings to separate alcohol-related metabolic changes from primary frontotemporal hypometabolism.

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

sequence_constraints.reason: Exclude structural cause of focal cognitive symptoms and screen for elevated ICP before lumbar puncture.

critical_actions: Administer empiric thiamine and engage addiction medicine — alcohol use must be addressed irrespective of the primary diagnosis.
Re-evaluate cognitive course after sustained abstinence to distinguish residual alcohol-related deficit from progressive FTD.
Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
Do not attribute the entire syndrome to alcohol: the frontotemporal lobar pattern and behavioural phenotype indicate a primary neurodegenerative process.
key_reasoning_points: Frontotemporal lobar pattern + behavioural Rascovsky features point to bvFTD; alcohol is a comorbid contributor.
Thiamine replacement and abstinence are critical adjuncts.
Maternal early-onset dementia warrants a genetic panel.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Heavy alcohol use is a comorbidity; the lobar frontotemporal pattern is not explained by alcohol alone.

metadata.notes: Moderate bvFTD with concurrent alcohol use disorder. Key teaching: alcohol escalation may be a symptom of FTD disinhibition; FDG-PET after sobriety period isolates primary FTD changes; disulfiram contraindicated in FTD due to impaired impulse control.
